items.headline: Latest confirmed close: stocks fell again Nov. 17, with AI worries behind a fourth straight loss
items.note: The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, the Dow fell 1.64% to 50,759.42 and the Nasdaq fell 0.74% to 24,328.38, with AI chip and software worries weighing on tech. I couldn't find a confirmed Nov. 18 close, so check a markets site for Wednesday's move.

items.headline: Nvidia posts $115.8B quarter and guides to about $130B
items.note: Reported Nov. 17: adjusted EPS of $2.68 vs. about $2.48 expected, and revenue of $115.8B vs. about $109B expected. Q4 guidance of about $130B assumes no China data center compute revenue, and gross margin is guided down to 71–72%. It's the first report since Jensen Huang's departure as CEO; CFO Colette Kress is running the company during the search.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO is set to price Nov. 18, with trading as ANT slated for today
items.note: The plan is 825 million shares at $70–$78, and several outlets reported it may price above that range. I couldn't find the final price or first-day trading, so treat the numbers as pre-pricing. A second $26B private placement is planned at the IPO price.

items.headline: Anthropic's valuation at the range is reported at roughly $1.3–$1.4 trillion
items.note: Reports (Reuters, Bloomberg and others, per a secondary summary) put the valuation near that level, and estimates vary by source and by whether you count fully diluted shares. It would make this one of the largest tech listings ever and a gauge of appetite for AI labs.

items.headline: Wholesale inflation ran hotter than expected last week; Nvidia sold off on China trade tensions
items.note: On Nov. 13 the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower while the Dow edged up, though all three still ended the week higher. Hotter wholesale inflation data and renewed U.S.–China trade friction weighed on Nvidia ahead of its earnings.

items.headline: Fed's Bowman says inflation has lasted longer than hoped and is the top priority
items.note: In remarks on Nov. 10 she said growth is stronger and the labor market is stabilizing, but inflation pressures have persisted and recently shown signs of broadening. The Fed held rates steady at its Oct. 28 meeting, so rate cuts that would help growth stocks look less certain.

items.headline: Tech hiring is selective: modest October gains, and data science is holding up better than most roles
items.note: CompTIA-based reports show the tech sector added about 7,200 jobs in October, with hiring momentum pausing in November and more selective employers. Interview Query argues specialized data skills stand out, though layoffs still hit many tech fields, so a strong ML portfolio matters for internships.

items.headline: NYC startups had a record second quarter, and frontier AI work is starting to show up in the city
items.note: AlleyWatch reports NYC startups raised $8.88B across 233 deals in Q2 2026, up 46% year over year, with AI apps and fintech among the leaders. Two frontier-model funding rounds in June suggest AI development is no longer only a San Francisco story, which is good news for NYC internship hunting.

learn.explain: A private placement is when a company sells shares directly to a small group of big investors instead of to the public on a stock exchange. It usually happens faster and with less paperwork than an IPO. Anthropic planned a $26 billion private placement of a separate class of stock at the same price as its IPO, alongside the public offering. Buyers in private placements often can't resell right away. The company gets cash either way, but existing shareholders own a slightly smaller slice of it afterward.
learn.try: Look up the difference between a public offering and a private placement in an S-1 filing's 'Plan of Distribution' section.
